attribution_limitations: Distribution of the September 2018 opacities differs: the text describes new patchy ground-glass opacities in bilateral lobes, while the Figure 2A caption says the new patchy opacity was in the irradiated area of the right hilum and did not occur outside the irradiated area. The irradiated field is not described, so this is recorded as an ambiguity rather than a conflict.

Pleural effusion laterality conflicts: the text says a small right pleural effusion on the CT after nivolumab, the Figure 3B caption says a small left pleural effusion. The bilateral ground-glass finding is not disputed.

Timing differs between text and Figure 3 caption: the text places improvement on day 15 and recurrence on day 24, while the caption says corticosteroid for 1 week to resolution and recurrence "Ten days later". The anchors are different or unstated.

The case text says she was thought to develop immunotherapy-related pneumonitis; the abstract, the Figure 3B caption and the discussion state it more firmly. Recorded as provisional per the case-text wording.

The negation list "did not experience other causes of obstructive lung disease, autoimmune disease, organ transplant, smoke inhalation, or medications" is itemised for other causes of obstructive lung disease, autoimmune disease, organ transplant and smoke inhalation; medications is not itemised because the source does not say which medications are meant, and the patient did receive chemotherapy.

Dates are stated only as months; Figure 1 prints further month-level dates and cycle counts inside the image (pixel content in visual.json only). The text gives no dates for the June 2019 pneumonitis course after nivolumab, only day counts with no stated anchor.

Time axis of anti-tumor treatment and intervention on pneumonitis. Line graph illustrating disease progression, anti-tumor therapy, pneumonitis and intervention from April 2018 to August 2019. IVIG, Intravenous immunoglobulin; SVCS, Superior vena cava obstruction syndrome.

(A) After receiving three-dimensional thoracic radiotherapy, a CT scan showed new patchy opacity developed in the irradiated area of hilum of the right lung, which did not occur outside the irradiated area.
(B) This patient initiated steroid treatment, pneumonitis was partially resolved within 1 month, with a significantly clinical improvement.
(C) Pulmonary inflammation disappeared 2 months later.
(A) A CT scan showed no any inflammatory lesions in the lungs following the treatment with first PD-L1 inhibitor atezolizumab.
(B) Nivolumab was started when this patient progressed on atezolizumab treatment. A CT scan indicated new patchy ground-grass opacities in the bilateral lungs, with a small left pleural effusion.
(C) After treatment with corticosteroid for 1 week, this patient's symptom improved significantly, with a radiologic complete resolution of the ground-glass opacities and the pleural effusion.
(D) Ten days later, a CT scan showed reoccurred pneumonitis, of grade 3 severity.
(E) High-dose intravenous corticosteroid therapy did not alleviate her symptoms within 5 days, with worsening radiographic findings.

(F) After she received immunosuppressive agents including infliximab, mycophenolate mofetil and human immunoglobulin, fever, dry cough, and dyspnea were relieved significantly, with a significant improvement of pulmonary inflammation.
